root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: Before the temporary encoded path is replaced and freed, any fragment state that survives past that replacement must already be represented by `u->fragment` instead of the local interior pointer `fragment`.
root_cause_criterion.criterion: At the dot-segment replacement site in `seturl()`, once `strcmp(newp, path)` selects a replacement and `path_alloced` permits freeing the temporary encoded path, the fragment state that remains live after this point must already be the handle-owned `u->fragment` state. Keeping the later fragment state in local `fragment` carries an interior alias into storage whose lifetime ends at `free(path)`.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original reaches the replacement-free site with `retained_fragment_state_ptr` still equal to local `fragment` while `u->fragment` is NULL, so later fragment handling remains tied to the temporary path allocation that is about to be released. The fixed original reaches the same site with `retained_fragment_state_ptr == u->fragment == NULL`, proving post-normalization fragment state no longer depends on the local interior alias when the free executes.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: In the vulnerable original trace, `path_replace_free.retained_fragment_state_ptr=0x60300003181b` and `path_replace_free.owned_fragment_ptr=(nil)` while the protected replacement-free event executes. In the fixed clean trace, the same event executes twice and both times records `retained_fragment_state_ptr == owned_fragment_ptr == (nil)`.

nodes.state: At the replacement branch, the raw local `fragment` pointer still aliases bytes inside the temporary encoded `path` buffer whose lifetime ends at `free(path)`. That raw alias is the stale interior pointer later consumed by the crash path.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `path_replace_free.fragment_alias_ptr=0x60300003181b`, and the verified transition carries that exact pointer value to the later stale read.

nodes.state: The post-normalization `if(fragment && fragment[0])` condition dereferences the same local `fragment` alias, producing the AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free READ 1.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace reaches `fragment_read_sink` immediately before the ASan report and records the same pointer value later blamed by the sanitizer.

edges.relation: The exact local `fragment` pointer captured when the temporary encoded path is replaced and freed is later the `fragment` argument dereferenced by `if(fragment && fragment[0])` on the crashing vulnerable path.
edges.evidence: In the vulnerable original trace, `path_replace_free.fragment_alias_ptr == fragment_read_sink.fragment_argument_ptr == 0x60300003181b` with ordered event indices 1 -> 2.
